reflection.quote: We are what we repeatedly do. Excellence, then, is not an act, but a habit.
reflection.reading:
It's a Tuesday in August. Not a milestone, not a crisis, not a chip anniversary. Just a Tuesday. And that's the part nobody tells you about when you're still drinking — that most of your life is going to happen on Tuesdays. The bulk of it. The Tuesday where you go to work, cook something for dinner, text a friend back, go to bed at a reasonable hour. When I was drunk, I treated Tuesdays like a holding cell between weekends. Something to survive, or numb, or skip past. I lost years to that math.

The strange gift of sobriety is that a regular Tuesday stops being empty. It becomes the actual thing — the raw material your life is built out of. The workout you did this morning. The coffee you actually tasted. The conversation with your coworker where you were fully there instead of hungover and half-checked-out. None of it makes for a good story. All of it is the story.

Durant's line about Aristotle sits with me because it takes the pressure off the grand gestures. You don't have to be excellent today. You just have to do the small things that, stacked up, become a life. Show up. Eat something. Call the friend. Go to bed sober. Tuesday is not a rehearsal for something bigger. This is it. And that turns out to be enough.
reflection.meditation: Where can I be more present in the ordinary parts of today?

affirmations: I am building a life out of ordinary days, and that is enough.
Today I can be fully present for the small things without needing to escape them.
I have the agency to choose what happens next, one decision at a time.

gratitude.prayer: Grateful for a quiet Tuesday I can actually be inside of. Grateful for the version of me that kept showing up long enough to get here — through the shaky early days, the boring middle, the ordinary now. Grateful that my life is no longer something I need a break from.
gratitude.closing: One more day, clear-eyed. That's the whole thing.
